**8B.7 Research Note, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, 2024**

**Overall read**
- Mixed, leaning negative on realized outcomes.
- The macro trajectory moved partly in the direction Tinubu said he wanted: fiscal credibility improved, FX distortions narrowed, and reserves/market functioning got better.
- But the lived-outcome side lagged badly: inflation stayed very high, food insecurity worsened, and the August protest wave showed that many Nigerians experienced the reform path as acute hardship rather than shared improvement.

**Accepted claims**
- **IMF says Nigeria inherited a weak macro position, but the government launched a coherent stabilization package**
  - Publisher: IMF
  - Date: 2024-02-09
  - URL: https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/02/09/pr2443-nigeria-imf-exec-board-concludes-pfa
  - Summary: The IMF said Tinubu’s government moved ahead with subsidy removal, FX unification, a fiscal/tax reform committee, and palliatives to soften the shock. This supports the idea that the administration was pursuing a real policy path, but it also frames 2024 as a transition with heavy adjustment costs rather than a completed success.
  - Question IDs: `8B.7`
  - Also informs: `8B.6`

- **World Bank says macro conditions improved, but household pain remained severe**
  - Publisher: World Bank
  - Date: 2024-06-13
  - URL: https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/06/13/turning-the-corner-nigeria-ongoing-path-of-economic-reforms
  - Summary: The Bank reported improved FX supply and a smaller official/parallel rate gap, but also said reforms intensified cost-of-living pressures and inflation reached 33.7 percent in April 2024. That is strong mixed evidence: the direction improved on some core macro indicators, but not yet on everyday welfare.
  - Question IDs: `8B.7`
  - Also informs: `8B.6`

- **World Bank says reforms improved reserves, fiscal health, and stability, but inflation stayed high**
  - Publisher: World Bank
  - Date: 2024-10-17
  - URL: https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/17/nigeria-staying-the-course-on-reforms-progress-amidst-challenges
  - Summary: The Bank said reforms since May 2023 had improved macro stability, fiscal health, and reserves, and reduced debt-related risks. It still emphasized that households and businesses were facing pain and that inflation remained elevated. This is the strongest late-year positive evidence for directional movement, but it is still incomplete and conditional.
  - Question IDs: `8B.7`
  - Also informs: `8B.6`

- **Reuters reports inflation and living-cost pressure worsened after the reform shock**
  - Publisher: Reuters via Investing.com
  - Date: 2024-08-01
  - URL: https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hundreds-gather-across-nigerian-cities-to-protest-cost-of-living-crisis-3548376
  - Summary: Reuters reported subsidy removal, naira devaluation, and higher electricity tariffs pushed inflation above 34 percent and fueled nationwide cost-of-living protests. This is strong negative evidence that the public outcome in 2024 was not yet moving cleanly in the intended welfare direction.
  - Question IDs: `8B.7`
  - Also informs: `8B.6`

- **Reuters reports acute food insecurity reached massive scale**
  - Publisher: Reuters via Investing.com
  - Date: 2024-08-27
  - URL: https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/insecurity-rising-costs-push-31-million-nigerians-into-acute-food-shortage-study-says-3589474
  - Summary: Reuters reported that 31.8 million Nigerians were acutely food insecure, with subsidy removal and insecurity cited as major drivers. This is the clearest negative outcome item in the record for Tinubu’s stated goals around hardship reduction and prosperity.
  - Question IDs: `8B.7`
  - Also informs: `8B.6`

- **Government resumed cash transfers to vulnerable households**
  - Publisher: Reuters via MarketScreener
  - Date: 2024-02-26
  - URL: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Nigeria-restarts-cash-transfers-to-cushion-hardship-caused-by-reforms-46031196/
  - Summary: The government approved direct cash transfers to 12 million vulnerable households to cushion reform pain. This is real implementation in the intended direction, but it is compensatory relief, not evidence that the broader economic outcome had already improved.
  - Question IDs: `8B.7`
  - Also informs: `8B.6`

- **Student-loan reform was turned into a standing access mechanism**
  - Publisher: State House
  - Date: 2024-04-04
  - URL: https://statehouse.gov.ng/in-detail-the-student-loan-access-to-higher-education-act-2024/
  - Summary: The student-loan pledge became a signed law and delivery structure via NELFUND. This is positive directional evidence for access to education and human capital, but in 2024 it is still mainly design-and-launch evidence, not outcome evidence.
  - Question IDs: `8B.7`
  - Also informs: `8B.6`

- **World Bank funding targeted health, education governance, and resilience infrastructure**
  - Publisher: World Bank
  - Date: 2024-09-26
  - URL: https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/09/26/world-bank-approves-new-financing-for-nigeria-to-improve-health-outcomes-safety-of-dams-and-irrigation-services
  - Summary: The package targeted health, basic education governance, and resilience infrastructure, implying that the reform path was being backed with instruments that could improve outcomes over time. The main limitation is lag: these are medium-term channels, not proof of 2024 results.
  - Question IDs: `8B.7`
  - Also informs: `8B.6`

- **Education safety outcomes remained weak**
  - Publisher: Human Rights Watch
  - Date: 2024-04-11
  - URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/11/nigeria-10-years-after-chibok-schoolchildren-still-risk
  - Summary: HRW said authorities had failed to sustain safe-learning measures and children remained at risk of abduction. This is negative evidence that, despite policy rhetoric on human capital and child protection, the outcome direction had not yet improved in a meaningful way for vulnerable children.
  - Question IDs: `8B.7`
  - Also informs: `8B.6`

- **Girls and young women escaping Boko Haram still faced abuse and weak reintegration**
  - Publisher: Amnesty International
  - Date: 2024-06-09
  - URL: https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/nigeria-girls-failed-by-authorities-after-escaping-boko-haram-captivity-new-report/
  - Summary: Amnesty documented unlawful detention and weak reintegration support for girls and young women who escaped Boko Haram captivity. That cuts hard against any claim that 2024 outcomes were moving toward better protection for vulnerable groups.
  - Question IDs: `8B.7`
  - Also informs: `8B.6`

- **Protest crackdown shows worsening political-security outcomes**
  - Publisher: Amnesty International
  - Date: 2024-11-28
  - URL: https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/
  - Summary: Amnesty documented killings, mass detentions, and torture during the August crackdown. Even if the protests were about hardship and corruption, the state response made the outcome picture worse, not better, for civic safety and public trust.
  - Question IDs: `8B.7`
  - Also informs: `8B.6`

- **Late corrective action on detained minors is real, but reactive**
  - Publisher: TheCable
  - Date: 2024-11-04
  - URL: https://www.thecable.ng/tinubu-orders-probe-of-security-agents-involved-in-arrest-detention-of-minors/
  - Summary: Tinubu ordered an investigation into the arrest and treatment of minors detained over the protests and said officers could face discipline. This is a real corrective step, but it came after visible abuse, so it does not erase the earlier negative outcome trend.
  - Question IDs: `8B.7`
  - Also informs: `8B.6`

**Search gap**
- I found good evidence on macro direction, compensation, and social protection, plus strong evidence that living conditions worsened for many people in 2024.
- I did not find a clean end-of-year independent evaluation for the student-loan system, cash transfers, procurement reform, or resettlement scheme showing measured 2024 outcome gains at national scale.
- So the best-supported judgment is: the direction improved at the macro-policy level, but the realized welfare and security outcomes were still mixed to negative by late 2024.
